_comment: Structural exceptions for sbsi-docx-format-core's validator/normalizer, discovered by inspecting this template's actual OOXML (word/document.xml, word/styles.xml). Every value below is the engine's own generic default — listed explicitly so future template registrations have a concrete example to copy and edit, and so a reviewer can see at a glance what was verified against the real file rather than assumed.
_cover_page_strategy_note: Verified: paragraph 'Số: .../QĐ-TGĐ, Hà Nội, ngày...' (the promulgation-page opener) has <w:pageBreakBefore/>, immediately after the cover + doc-info table + TOC on page 1. Everything before it is excluded from ordinary-text/numbering checks.
_appendix_heading_pattern_note: Verified: 'Phụ lục số: NN' paragraphs mark each appendix (Danh mục tài liệu tham khảo uses manually-numbered '1. ... 2. ...' legal citations with no numPr — tolerated as a WARNING, not blocking, inside this zone).
_structural_heading_patterns_note: No additions needed: every real Chương/Điều paragraph in this template carries a DIRECT per-paragraph <w:outlineLvl> override (0 for Chương, 1 for Điều — see known_style_hierarchy below for why this is NOT simply 'the style's outline level'), so the engine's generic default Chương/Điều text-pattern check correctly never fires as a false positive on real headings here. It DOES correctly fire on a paragraph that uses Style1/Style2 but is MISSING that direct override and has the vocabulary typed as literal text — this is a real, observed failure mode (see 'chuong_structure' below), not a hypothetical.

known_style_hierarchy._note: IMPORTANT, corrected 2026-08-17 after a real bug was traced to trusting the wrong claim here: outline level 0/1 does NOT come from the style definitions themselves. Style1 has no outlineLvl in its OWN <w:style> block at all; Style2's own style-level outlineLvl is 9, which OOXML/this engine's effective_outline() treats as 'Body Text', i.e. NOT a heading. The real outline 0/1 comes from a DIRECT <w:outlineLvl> override present on every individual Chương/Điều paragraph's own <w:pPr>, layered on top of the style. A paragraph that uses pStyle=Style2 but omits this direct override resolves to outline 9 -> not a heading -> is correctly reported as [Headings] Manual/non-structural heading text if its typed text also matches the Chương/Điều vocabulary pattern. Always copy the outlineLvl from a real sibling paragraph when cloning, never assume the style alone provides it.

number_paragraph.numPr: inherited from Style1's own style definition (numId=5) — do NOT add a paragraph-level numId override, absence of one is what lets the style's active numbering render 'Chương I/II/III...' automatically

title_paragraph._numId_0_note: numId=0 is the explicit OOXML sentinel for 'no numbering on this paragraph' — required here so the title doesn't ALSO render a 'Chương N' prefix; only the empty number_paragraph immediately before it does.

chuong_structure.verified_example: Body paragraphs 60-61 in the real template: an empty Style1 paragraph (renders 'Chương I' from numId=5's numbering definition) immediately followed by a Style1 paragraph containing only 'QUY ĐỊNH CHUNG' with numId=0.
chuong_structure.real_bug_this_documents: A reformatted document (QT_Nghien_cuu_va_Phat_trien_SPDV_so, found 2026-08-17) built its new chapter headings as a SINGLE paragraph using pStyle=Style2 (wrong — should be Style1), no direct outlineLvl override, numId=0, and typed 'Chương I' literally as text. This is exactly the failure this manifest section exists to prevent a repeat of — see sbsi-docx-format-core's clone_structural_paragraph() helper, which builds this two-paragraph pattern correctly instead of leaving it to be hand-rolled per generation task.

dieu_numbering._note: Verified: every real Điều paragraph in this template (across all 4 chapters) shares the SAME numId=19 — Điều numbering runs continuously through the whole document (Điều 1, 2, 3... regardless of which Chương it falls under), it does NOT restart at 1 per chapter. When cloning a new Điều paragraph, reuse this numId from any existing Style2 sibling; do not invent a new numbering definition.

_toc_field_switches_note: Informational: confirms the TOC field is outline-level-driven (levels 1-3), consistent with Style1/Style2 mapping to outline 0/1.
known_rendering_caveat: LibreOffice (used by render_qa.py) did not clearly honor this template's paragraph-level 'numPr numId="0"' override on the Style1 heading the same way Word does during manual verification — treat render_qa.py's PDF/PNG output as a strong visual-QA proxy, not a guaranteed Word-identical render. Confirm final numbering appearance in real Word before high-stakes distribution.
